newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end higher on rate-cut hopes.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end higher on rate-cut hopes.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed higher on Monday on hopes that the central bank may loosen monetary policy further at its board meeting on Thursday, brokers said.
The index ended up 63.46 points or 1.00 percent at 6,435.43. Turnover was an active T$58.99 billion.
"Hopes for a rate cut boosted sentiment even though the index had already risen 1.3 percent on Saturday," said Alex Yang of National Securities.
The central bank has said it would review a proposal at the meeting to set a direction to lower banks' reserve requirements and at the same time raise the liquidity ratio.

Plastics rose 2.15 percent on late-morning news that industrial conglomerate BTR had sold off its majority stakes in three Taiwan petrochemical firms to raise some US$300 million in a corporate realignment.

Of the firms sold, Taita jumped by the daily seven percent limit, rising T$2 to T$31, Asia Polymer gained 50 cents or 0.93 percent to T$54.5 and China General Plastics, also rising the daily limit, gained T$1.9 to close at T$29.3.
Textiles were strong on price increases for polyester fibre products, with Shinkong Fibre up T$1 to T$23.5.
Paper shares rose on pulp price rises.
Financial shares rose 1.01 percent as any further central bank rate cut would benefit the sector most, with China Bills up 90 cents to T$27.2.
Electronics, which had led the market's rise in recent sessions, encountered consolidation, rising only 0.25 percent.
Brokers said some late-session selling offset earlier gains, indicating investors might use Tuesday to digest the rise.
"On Tuesday, the index will likely consolidate between 6,400 and 6,475 after two straight days of strong gains," Yang said.
